title: Trace Delivery ACK Coordinator for Multi-backend Retry and Idempotency
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a lightweight ACK coordination service that ensures reliable, idempotent delivery of spans to multiple tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party OTLP sinks). The coordinator serializes delivery attempts, tracks per-backend acknowledgement state, enforces retry/backoff policies, and provides deduplication helpers for downstream processors. Goals: 1) reduce duplicate spans and noisy traces when backends intermittently fail or retry; 2) provide clear delivery metrics and SLOs for span handoff; 3) keep operational complexity low (favor at-least-once with deterministic dedupe) so we can ship quickly and iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator deployed behind existing span-gateway and can be toggled per-tenant via runtime flag
Per-backend ack state exposed in Prometheus (delivery_ack_lag_seconds, delivery_retries_total, pending_delivery_count)
Duplicate spans rate reduced by >= 90% in synthetic failure tests compared to baseline direct-fanout
System respects per-backend ordering window for spans belonging to the same trace (configurable window up to 5s)
Fallback policy implemented: if primary backend fails repeatedly, traffic is routed to warm standby according to routing policy
End-to-end E2E test and a canary rollout plan documented in PRD and runbook
design_decisions: Use idempotency tokens (trace_id + span_seq + backend) to dedupe rather than trying full exactly-once semantics
State kept in small Redis hash per-tenant for fast lookups; durability via periodic checkpoints to S3 as compressed WAL
Backoff uses jittered exponential with per-backend backpressure signals to avoid cascading failures
Prefer soft-ack (backend acknowledged receipt) vs hard-ack (backend processed) to keep latency SLOs reasonable
Coordinator runs colocated with span gateway as a separate process to reduce cross-cluster traffic
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype ack table API and small in-memory coordinator (2d)
Integration: wire prototype into span-gateway fanout path and add tests (3d)
Durability: implement Redis-backed state + WAL checkpointing to S3 (4d)
Metrics + dashboards: add Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard for per-backend delivery health (2d)
Canary rollout: feature-flag per-tenant, monitor for duplicates and latency, gradual ramp (3d)
Postmortem and follow-ups: tune dedupe windows, add optional strong-consistency mode for enterprise customers
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coordinator becomes a new availability bottleneck. Mitigation: design stateless API endpoints for reads, horizontal shard by tenant, graceful degradation to direct-fanout when coordinator unavailable
Risk: Redis hot keys for high-volume tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant sharding and move heavy tenants to dedicated Redis nodes; add sampling for very high-volume traces
Risk: Increased end-to-end latency. Mitigation: soft-ack strategy and per-request timeout budget; surface latency budget in the Console and allow per-tenant SLO overrides
